title: Uranus: Ultra-efficient Acceleration Architecture for the Privacy Inference of Graph Neural Networks
problem: Fully Homomorphic Encryption enables secure GNN inference on encrypted data, but high computational costs make it impractical without dedicated accelerators. Existing CKKS-based GNN approaches require large encryption parameters; PPGNN combines CKKS with TFHE for memory efficiency but TFHE's SISD computing causes severe computational overhead.
motivation: Privacy-preserving GNN deployment on cloud platforms requires efficient FHE-based inference; existing approaches have prohibitive computational or memory costs.
method: Uranus uses a split encryption strategy: CKKS (a compression-friendly encryption scheme) for linear layers where approximate arithmetic works, and BFV (a scheme preserving exact integer values) for nonlinear activation functions that need precision, both with reduced encryption parameters sized for hardware. The hardware accelerator is highly reconfigurable to handle this mixed workload and maximize utilization by strategically balancing computation speed, memory use, and accuracy.
key_novelty: Uranus is the first accelerator that combines software and hardware design for encrypted graph neural networks (fully homomorphic encryption), achieving 92× speedup versus CKKS-only methods and 3.3–4.2× speedup versus PPGNN, with 119× better energy efficiency.
contributions: Hybrid FHE framework (CKKS+BFV) enabling SIMD-based efficient nonlinear computations
Reduced encryption parameter requirements improving hardware feasibility
Reconfigurable hardware accelerator maximizing computation throughput
92× speedup vs. CKKS, 3.3-4.2× vs. PPGNN, 119× energy vs. PPGNN
limitations: Evaluation on GNN models only; applicability to other FHE workloads unclear; parameter tuning for different graph sizes not discussed.
